origin:
The story of Porsche Penske Motorsport at the amateur level is an unusual one, born not from ambition to conquer the world of motorsport, but rather as a skunkworks project fueled by passion. It began in a small, unassuming garage in Weissach, Germany, where a group of Porsche engineers, led by the ambitious but unproven Klaus-Dieter Schmidt, tinkered with a dilapidated 944 Turbo after hours. Their goal wasn't fame or fortune, but a shared desire to prove that even a seemingly outdated platform could still punch above its weight class. 

Roger Penske, intrigued by the dedication and ingenuity of the team, offered the use of some of Penske's old testing facilities in the United States. This collaboration was the first time Porsche Penske Motorsport had ventured outside of Germany. This early support, though limited, proved crucial. The team's initial outings were a mix of triumphs and tribulations, often overshadowed by the sheer dominance of better-funded, professionally run operations. However, the 'Porsche Penske' name, even at this level, carried a certain weight, a promise of engineering excellence and unwavering determination.
philosophy: Porsche Penske Motorsport's amateur philosophy centers around continuous improvement and a relentless pursuit of efficiency. Car development is a collaborative effort, relying heavily on driver feedback and data analysis, with a strong emphasis on reliability and maximizing the performance of readily available components. The team culture is one of camaraderie and mutual respect, where every member, from the lead engineer to the tire specialist, is valued for their contribution. They believe that a well-oiled machine, both literally and figuratively, can overcome the limitations of a smaller budget.
achievements: Class win at the Nürburgring VLN Endurance Championship (2018)
Podium finish at the 24 Hours of Barcelona (2020)
Multiple regional championship titles in the German Endurance Series (various years)
Development of innovative data logging system for amateur racing teams

teamPrincipal.name: Klaus-Dieter Schmidt
teamPrincipal.background: Schmidt, a former Porsche engineer with a knack for problem-solving, leads the team with a hands-on approach. He fosters a collaborative environment, encouraging experimentation and learning from mistakes, even when it strains the limited resources.

keyFigures.name: Elke Hartmann
keyFigures.description: Hartmann's meticulous planning and insightful race strategy have often allowed the team to outmaneuver their rivals, despite their limited resources.

keyFigures.name: Jean-Pierre Dubois
keyFigures.description: Dubois's encyclopedic knowledge of Porsche vehicles and his ability to coax maximum performance from aging components are invaluable to the team's success.

headquarters: The team operates out of a modest workshop on the outskirts of Weissach, Germany. The facilities are basic but functional, reflecting the team's no-frills approach to racing. The workshop features a small dyno and a limited selection of spare parts.
fanBase: The team has a small but fiercely loyal following, primarily consisting of local Porsche enthusiasts and amateur racing aficionados who appreciate their dedication and ingenuity. They are seen as a symbol of grassroots motorsport, proving that passion and hard work can sometimes overcome financial constraints.
